title: Your Heart Doesn't Need Your Brain
sources: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker: its cells depolarize on their own (automaticity) and start every heartbeat without a signal from the brain (StatPearls, 'Physiology, Sinoatrial Node')
A normal resting heart rate is about 60 to 100 beats per minute, roughly one beat per second (American Heart Association)
The electrical impulse spreads from the SA node across the atria and through the AV node to the ventricles, making the heart contract (StatPearls, 'Physiology, Cardiac Conduction System')
The brain only adjusts the rate through the autonomic nerves: sympathetic nerves speed it up, the vagus nerve slows it down; a transplanted (denervated) heart still beats (StatPearls)
Donor hearts can be transported warm and beating in organ care systems such as the TransMedics OCS Heart ('heart in a box'), FDA approved 2021
The embryonic heart begins beating around day 22 after conception, before the brain controls it (Tan & Lewandowski, 'The Transitional Heart', 2020)

lines.text: Your heart doesn't need your brain to beat. It can even beat outside your body.
lines.caps: Your *heart | doesn't need | your *brain | to *beat | It can even beat | *outside your body

lines.text: That's because it has its own spark plug, a tiny patch of cells called the S. A. node.
lines.caps: That's because | it has its own | *spark plug | a *tiny patch | of cells | called the *SA node

lines.text: About once every second, it fires an electric spark.
The spark spreads across the heart, and the whole thing squeezes.
lines.caps: The spark *spreads | across the heart | and the whole thing | *squeezes

lines.text: Your brain can only speed it up or slow it down. It doesn't start the beat.
lines.caps: Your brain can only | *speed it up | or *slow it down | It *doesn't start | the beat

lines.text: So doctors can carry a donor heart in a machine, still warm and beating.

lines.text: And yours has been beating on its own since before you were even born.
